kind.description: message-kind for a value of an inbox line's kind field, directive for a value of a directive's command field, outbox-status for a value of an outbox line's status field, inbox-field and outbox-field for a field of each file's lines.

name.description: The value as a line carries it, or the field's name.

resumable.description: For a directive, whether a resume directive may name it as its target; null for every other value.

writer.description: For an outbox status, who appends a record of it: pass (one of the drive's passes) or driver (drive.ts itself); null for every other value.

type.description: For a field, the JSON type of its value: string, integer or boolean; null for every other value.

carriedBy.description: For a field, the kinds or statuses of the lines that carry it, each with always or sometimes, as `note (always), directive (sometimes)`; a line of a kind not named never carries it. Null for every other value.

meaning.description: What it means to a reader that writes or reads the mailbox, and what that reader does with it.

values.name: note
values.meaning: Context for the drive's passes, which they may read (`mailbox.ts check`) and acknowledge; it never controls the drive. A note that lacks a field a note always carries is dropped with a warning; a line that is not valid JSON, or a note that carries `command`, `target` or `generation`, is read as a malformed directive and holds the drive's pushes. `mailbox.ts repair` removes the interrupted line; a note that parses but carries a directive field stays until a person edits or removes it.

values.name: directive
values.meaning: A command the drive enforces mechanically, named in its `command` field. A directive line that does not parse holds the drive's pushes and ends the driver at its next checkpoint with exit 1, as an unreadable inbox does, and a re-armed drive ends again until a person repairs the file: `mailbox.ts repair` removes a line that is not valid JSON, while valid JSON of the wrong shape needs a person to correct or remove it.

values.name: hold-push
values.meaning: Holds every push the drive makes through `guarded-push.ts`: the push is refused with exit 17 (`PUSH_HELD`) until a `resume` with target `hold-push`. The drive goes on with its rounds.

values.name: pause
values.meaning: Holds the driver at its next checkpoint, keeping its locks, until a `resume` with target `pause`; one that lasts past `DRIVE_PR_PAUSE_MAX_SEC` ends the drive with exit 19 (`MAILBOX_PAUSE_TIMEOUT`).

values.name: stop
values.meaning: Ends the driver at its next checkpoint with exit 18 (`MAILBOX_STOPPED`), after any running pass finishes; one that also carries `now` ends it at once, cancelling the running pass, with exit 143. One naming a `generation` ends that driver alone; one naming none ends every later driver in the working tree too, until a `resume` with target `stop`.

values.name: resume
values.meaning: Clears the directive its `target` names. With target `stop` it also withdraws every stop addressed to a generation.

values.name: received
values.meaning: A pass saw the inbox message the record's `id` names (`mailbox.ts ack`), and has not answered it; the message is no longer shown as unseen.

values.name: done
values.meaning: A pass answered the inbox message the record's `id` names (`mailbox.ts respond`); the answer is in `response`.

values.name: ack
values.meaning: The driver of the record's `generation` acted on the `stop` or `pause` directive the record's `id` names, so a sender sees the directive took effect.

values.name: id
values.meaning: The message's identifier, unique in the inbox; an outbox record names it in its own `id`.

values.name: ts
values.meaning: When the message was sent, as an ISO 8601 time.

values.name: kind
values.meaning: One of the message kinds listed above.

values.name: from
values.meaning: Who sent it: a person's or a session's name, as the sender gives it.

values.name: pr
values.meaning: The number of the pull request the message is for, as nonzero decimal digits with no leading zero (`12`, never `012` or `0`); a drive reads only its own pull request's messages, and a directive whose `pr` is not in that form holds the drive's pushes.

values.name: body
values.meaning: The note's text, or a directive's reason.

values.name: command
values.meaning: One of the directives listed above.

values.name: target
values.meaning: The directive a `resume` clears; carried by every `resume` and by no other directive.

values.name: generation
values.meaning: The driver generation a `stop` addresses, a positive whole number the driver prints at its start; only a `stop` carries it.

values.name: now
values.meaning: Always `true` where present, and only beside a `generation`: the driver cancels its running pass at once rather than waiting for it, and exits 143 (`drives.ts --stop`).

values.name: id
values.meaning: The `id` of the inbox message the record answers.

values.name: ts
values.meaning: When the record was written, as an ISO 8601 time.

values.name: pr
values.meaning: The number of the pull request the record is for: a record acknowledges only that pull request's message.

values.name: status
values.meaning: One of the outbox statuses listed above.

values.name: response
values.meaning: A pass's answer, never empty; only a `done` record carries it.

values.name: generation
values.meaning: The generation of the driver that acted on the directive.
